correctness.rationale: For three ordered distinct targets the witness-weighted product D_i D_j D_k sums exactly over one incoming comparison per target. A constraint pattern on v involved points has probability p^d, with p the linear-extension fraction for one uniform coordinate. I independently generated witness identifications by restricted-growth labels and counted extensions by a subset recursion (replay: python3 /workspace/branches/verify4_private.py). The three-edge maxima for v=3,4,5,6 are 0, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8; only the single external common predecessor achieves 1/4 at v=4, and all other v=4 patterns have p≤1/8. The disjoint-pair and common-predecessor terms have exactly (n)_6 and (n)_4 embeddings for ordered targets. They give λ³ and λ². In removing extra choices, D−1_{D≥1}≤binom(D,2), and telescoping the product bounds the difference by the four-edge pattern count with two distinct predecessors at one target. Its maxima are 0, 1/8, 3/20, 1/9, 1/12 at v=3 through 7, all with 2^v p²<1. Thus every error tends to zero when d=2 log₂ n+O(1). The advertised counts 51 and 124 reproduce for the script's relabelled keys; if one takes a full quotient by external relabelling there are 37 and 62 classes instead. This convention does not affect coverage or maxima. Continuous common marginals can be reduced coordinatewise with no ties almost surely. Weak convergence plus the different limit of E(N)_3 establishes failure of uniform integrability of the third factorial powers.

evidence: For the edge count, three disjoint pairs and both uniform orientations of the three-leaf star have the critical powers; the out-star and the in-star each contribute λ². On four vertices every other feasible three-edge pattern is a nonuniform star or a path, with single-coordinate probability below 1/4. At five vertices the bound is (1/3)(1/2), and on three vertices the bound is 1/6. This independently checks the distinct λ³+2λ² edge normalization without assigning its priority.
The vertex proof keeps only stars with a common predecessor; it still needs the separate four-edge bound to justify pruning extra choices in an unbounded moment.

value.rationale: The defect is at the first higher factorial moment not controlled by the known two-moment Poisson approximation. It identifies a concrete rare three-target configuration and distinguishes the vertex count from the apparently interchangeable edge count. This explains a natural limitation of sparse-limit approximations, rather than adding only a numerical coefficient to a known convergence theorem.
